claims.claim: Writing Q for the nonzero squares and K_p=complement(H_p), both H_p and K_p are Cayley graphs on the multiplicative group Q. Their connection sets S and T have sizes (p−5)/4 and (p−1)/4, respectively.
claims.evidence: For x,y∈Q, χ(x−y)=χ(x/y−1), so adjacency depends only on x/y. The sets S={q≠1:χ(q−1)=1} and T={q:χ(q−1)=−1} are inverse-closed. Moreover Σ_{q∈Q}χ(q−1)=½(Σ_{x≠0}χ(x−1)+Σ_xχ(x(x−1)))=½(−1−1)=−1. Together with |S|+|T|=|Q|−1=(p−3)/2, this gives the claimed sizes, including p=5.
claims.search_method: Direct quadratic-character calculation, with q=1 and the smallest eligible prime checked explicitly.

claims.claim: The localized Paley sign matrix B has operator norm at most √p, by an exact conference-matrix identity.
claims.evidence: For C_{xy}=χ(x−y), character correlation gives C²=pI−J. Ordering F_p as {0},Q,{ν/q:q∈Q} for a nonsquare ν gives the stated blocks. Its Q,Q block is J+B²+D²=pI−J, hence B²+D²=pI−2J. Therefore ||Bv||²=p||v||²−2(1ᵀv)²−||Dv||²≤p||v||² for every real v.
claims.search_method: Exact block-matrix multiplication and quadratic-character correlation.

claims.claim: θ(K_p) is exactly an explicit finite Fourier linear program, or equivalently a nonnegative-vector problem for a half-dimensional Fourier projection.
claims.evidence: Averaging over the regular Q-action preserves feasibility and objective and yields X_{xy}=f(x⁻¹y)/n. Trace and edge constraints become f(1)=1 and f|_T=0; positive semidefiniteness is exactly f̂(ψ)≥0, with conjugate-character coordinates equal. Setting y_ψ=f̂(ψ)/n gives y≥0, Σy=1, and objective n y_triv. Fourier inversion shows support on D={1}∪S is equivalent to membership in the range of the orthogonal Fourier projection P_D. Since |D|=(p−1)/4=n/2, this is the asserted half-dimensional formulation, and the construction is reversible.
claims.search_method: Automorphism averaging followed by exact finite-abelian Fourier diagonalization and inversion.

claims.claim: Every nontrivial Fourier eigenvalue of B is the real part of a Jacobi sum of modulus √p.
claims.evidence: For nontrivial ψ on Q, either extension A to F_p* is neither 1 nor χ. Up to conjugating ψ, the eigenvalue is R_ψ=½(J(A,χ)+J(Aχ,χ)). Gauss-sum identities give J(A,χ)J(Aχ,χ)=G(χ)²=p, while both factors have modulus √p because A,Aχ,χ and the relevant products are nontrivial. Thus the factors are conjugates and R_ψ=Re J(A,χ). This also checks the possible order-two ψ case and excludes only the trivial Fourier mode.
claims.search_method: Jacobi-sum expansion with all exceptional-character cases checked through Gauss-sum identities.

claims.claim: For every vertex-transitive graph G on n vertices, θ(G)θ(complement(G))=n.
claims.evidence: The dual is min t with M=tI+Z−J⪰0 and Z supported on edges. Then (M+J)/(nt) is primal-feasible for the complement and has objective at least n/t, proving the product is at least n. Conversely, average an optimal primal X over a transitive automorphism group. Then diag X=1/n and X1=(θ(G)/n)1. Consequently (n²/θ(G))X−J⪰0 and is a complement-dual certificate of value n/θ(G), proving the reverse inequality.
claims.search_method: Independent primal-dual SDP proof, including the automorphism averaging step.

claims.claim: Theta is monotone under taking induced subgraphs.
claims.evidence: Extending a feasible matrix for an induced subgraph by zero rows and columns preserves positive semidefiniteness, trace, objective, and every edge-zero constraint. Hence the induced subgraph's theta cannot exceed that of the original graph.
claims.search_method: Direct feasible-solution embedding in the defining SDP.

claims.claim: Theta is additive on disjoint unions: θ(G⊔L)=θ(G)+θ(L).
claims.evidence: In Gram form the objective is the squared norm of the sum of all Gram vectors. Scaling optimal families for G and L with trace shares proportional to θ(G),θ(L), and aligning their sum vectors, attains θ(G)+θ(L). Conversely, if the two block traces are a,b, their sum-vector norms are at most √(aθ(G)) and √(bθ(L)); triangle inequality and Cauchy–Schwarz give total objective at most (a+b)(θ(G)+θ(L))=θ(G)+θ(L).
claims.search_method: Two-sided Gram-representation proof with exact trace normalization.

claims.claim: The full Paley graph P_p satisfies θ(P_p)=√p.
claims.evidence: Translations act transitively on P_p, while multiplication by a nonsquare is an isomorphism from P_p to its complement. The verified vertex-transitive product identity therefore gives θ(P_p)²=p; positivity gives θ(P_p)=√p.
claims.search_method: Self-complementing isomorphism combined with the independently proved theta product identity.

claims.evidence: Multiplication by a nonsquare maps Q onto the nonsquares N and turns a nonsquare Q-difference into a square difference, so K_p≅P_p[N]. In P_p[{0}∪N], vertex 0 is isolated. Thus this induced graph is K_1⊔K_p and has theta 1+θ(K_p). Induced-subgraph monotonicity and θ(P_p)=√p give the result, including equality for p=5.
claims.search_method: Explicit field relabeling followed by induced-subgraph monotonicity and additivity.

claims.evidence: H_p is d=(p−5)/4 regular on n=(p−1)/2 vertices, and on 1⊥ its adjacency eigenvalues are (−1+R_ψ)/2. The B-norm bound gives the uniform lower spectral bound L=−(√p+1)/2. The dual certificate tI+cA−J with c=n/(d−L) and t=−nL/(d−L) is positive semidefinite, yielding t=(√p+1)²/(√p+3). This construction also works at p=5; equivalently H_5 is edgeless on two vertices and both sides equal 2.
claims.search_method: Exact adjacency-spectrum reduction and direct SDP dual-certificate verification, including p=5.

claims.evidence: The upper bound is claim 8. Since H_p is Cayley and hence vertex-transitive, θ(H_p)θ(K_p)=n. Dividing n=(p−1)/2 by the verified upper bound (√p+1)²/(√p+3) for θ(H_p) gives exactly (√p−1)(√p+3)/(2(√p+1)).
claims.search_method: Exact algebra applied to the independently verified product identity and one-sided bounds.

claims.claim: The proven bounds imply 1/√2≤liminf θ(K_p)/√(p/2)≤limsup θ(K_p)/√(p/2)≤√2, and isolate the unresolved step as asymptotic balance of the complementary theta numbers.
claims.evidence: After division by √(p/2), the lower and upper bounds tend respectively to 1/√2 and √2. Since θ(H_p)θ(K_p)=n=(p−1)/2, θ(K_p)/√n→1 is equivalent to θ(H_p)/√n→1 and, by positivity and the product constraint, to θ(H_p)−θ(K_p)=o(√p). The current interval allows both the target limit and alternatives, so the claimed unresolved balance is correctly identified.
claims.search_method: Exact asymptotic normalization and analysis of positive factors with fixed product.

claims.claim: The exact small-prime values are θ(K_5)=1, θ(K_13)=2, θ(K_17)=8−4√2; correspondingly θ(H_5)=2, θ(H_13)=3, and θ(H_17)=2+√2.
claims.evidence: The exact checker passed. For p=13, the feasible value a=1/2 gives objective 2, while the l=3 Fourier constraint gives the matching upper bound. For p=17, a=2−√2 and b=3−2√2 make all eight Fourier eigenvalues nonnegative; the positive combination (4−2√2)L_3+(3−2√2)L_4 certifies objective at most 8−4√2. The complementary values follow from products 2·3=6 and (8−4√2)(2+√2)=8; p=5 is directly K_2 versus the two-vertex edgeless graph.
claims.search_method: Exact Fourier primal/dual certificates over Q and Q(√2), plus direct modular construction; no floating-point comparisons.
claims.witness: p=13: a=1/2. p=17: (a,b)=(2−√2,3−2√2) with the stated positive dual combination. p=5: K_5=K_2 and H_5 is edgeless on two vertices.

claims.claim: A tempting exact explanation—K_p being a relabelled copy of H_p with one perfect matching added—is already false for p=17.
claims.evidence: The checker derives H_17=Cay(Z/8Z,{1,4,7}) and K_17=Cay(Z/8Z,{2,3,5,6}) directly from F_17, then exhausts all 14 perfect matchings of K_17. H_17 is triangle-free with four induced 4-cycles. Twelve matching deletions retain a triangle; the remaining two are triangle-free but each has six induced 4-cycles. These isomorphism invariants exclude H_17 in every case.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive integer enumeration of all perfect matchings, followed by exact triangle and induced-four-cycle counts.
claims.witness: At p=17 the only triangle-free deletions use matchings {(0,3),(1,6),(2,5),(4,7)} and {(0,5),(1,4),(2,7),(3,6)}; both residual graphs have six induced 4-cycles, whereas H_17 has four.

target_evidence: The exact target requires proving that θ(complement(H_p))/√(p/2) tends to 1, or proving that assertion false. The draft proves only the constant-factor interval [1/√2,√2] and equivalent formulations of the missing asymptotic balance; these results permit a limit of 1 as well as other behavior. They are correct, nonvacuous progress but do not settle the requested dichotomy, so target coverage is VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS. The draft labels its resolution PARTIAL and explicitly states that it does not prove the requested limit; therefore claimed_resolution is ACCURATE and the final writeup does not overclaim.
